reasoning_summary:
The record contains raw LaTeX source of Dogra, 'Unlikely intersections and the Chabauty-Kim method over number fields' (two excerpts: preamble/intro lines 0001-0124, and lines 0125-0842 covering the end of the unlikely-intersection proof, section 'The intersection of j_n(Z) with the Selmer variety', the metabelian machinery, and the proofs of Theorem 1.1 cases (1)-(3) plus the start of case (4)). I verified each mathematically substantive step in order.

Steps verified as justified:
(a) L.0135 dual connection formula: from nabla(e_{l_j}) = sum_i,k omega_i b_{ijk} e_{l_k} one gets nabla^*(e_{l_j}^*) = -sum b_{ikj} omega_i e_{l_k}^*, exactly as written.
(b) L.0191 vanishing 'b_{ijk}=0 if i>r_{n-2} and k<=r_{n-1}': with b_{ijk} = coefficient of e_k in [e_j,e_i] (the convention forced by the alpha_i formula at L.0189), nonvanishing forces deg(k)=deg(i)+1, so deg(i)>=n-1 implies k>r_{n-1}. Correct.
(c) L.0142/0162-0166 uniqueness-of-lift lemma: base case uses the hypothesis {h_1 dh_2} cap M_{n-1} = 0 correctly; the induction via 0->V'->V->V''->0 is valid.
(d) L.0261-0299 (Lemma W_bound_2): the filtered linear-algebra bookkeeping is consistent; the codimension inequality follows from the stated dimension additivity and the recursive kernel bound, with exactly j-i-1 kernel terms.
(e) L.0574 (Jannsen/global Euler characteristic): h^1 = h^0 + h^2 + sum_{v real} dim W^{c_v=-1} + (#P_C) dim W is the correct dimension form of Tate's formula (the complex place contributes -dim W because the normalized local factor is (#M)^2).
(f) L.0619-0623 (PTduality): combining (e) with Soule (h^2=0 for n>1) and h^0=0 gives dim H^1(G_{Q,T},W(n)) = dim (W(n))^{c=-1} = dim W^{c=1} for n odd, dim W^{c=-1} for n even. Correct.
(g) L.0451: dim H^1_f(G_{Q,T},W(1)) = dim W^{c=1} - dim W^{G_Q}. Checked against W trivial (0=1-1, units of Z), W = odd quadratic character (0=0-0), W = real quadratic character (1=1-0, rank of units of a real quadratic field mod units of Q).
(h) L.0438/0442: dim i_*Alb(Z)+rk i_*NS = dg + d(rho(J)-1) and rk(cap_sigma ...)^{c=1} - dim(...)^{G_Q} = (r_1+r_2-1)(rho(J)-1) are the correct counts for an induced module with c permuting embeddings.
(i) L.0605 weight argument in Lemma local_ignore: for X = P^1 - D one has U_1 = Q_p(1)^{#D-1}, so gr_i(U) really has weight -2i and the unramified H^1 and its dual both vanish for i>1.
(j) L.0738/0745 twists: U_1^{tensor(i-6)}(3) has weight -(i-6)-6 = -i matching gr_i(U_i), and H_1^{tensor(i-6)}(3) sits in H^{i-6}(X^{i-6}, Q_p(i-3)). Both consistent.
(k) L.0627-0645 (case (1)): for X = P^1-D, gr_i(U) = A_i(i) with A_i Artin, so dim H^1(G_{Q,T}, Wbar_i) = dim Wbar_i^{c=-1} exactly; combined with silly_injectivity (dim W_i^{c=-1} <= dim W_{i+1}^{c=1}) each summand is >=0 and infinitely many are >0, and Iwasawa kills the kernel terms for large i. The conclusion that the sum is unbounded is correct.
(l) L.0673-0689 (case (2), Bloch-Kato): W^*(1) sits in H^n(X^n,Q_p(1)), so 2r-1-n<0 and BK gives H^1_g=0; the constraint n>2 is exactly what makes W^*(1) have nonzero weight. Correct.
(m) L.0752-0770 (Lemma let_bla_be_as_in_bla): V -> Hom(im f_i, im f_{i+1}) is nonzero and Sp-equivariant hence injective since V is Sp-irreducible; the conjugation computations c[v,w]=-[v,w] => [v-c(v),w]=0 and the two-embedding computation c[P,Q]+[P,Q] = ([c(v_2)-v_1,c(w)],[v_2-c(v_1),w]) both check out (the latter exactly reproduces the displayed formula once the c=-1 lift is taken as (-c(w),w)).
(n) L.0780-0801 (case (3)): gr_i(Ubar_n) = Sym^{i-2}(V)(1) is correct for E-O (free metabelian on 2 generators, wedge^2 H_1(E) = Q_p(1)); the Iwasawa/Shapiro argument bounding H^1(G_{L,T},V_pi^{tensor i}) is valid.

The source is heavily typo-ridden (~18 clerical slips of identical character: repeated subscript at L.0108; 'surjection' for 'section' at L.0233; 'G_{Q,T}-stable' for 'G_{L,T}-stable' at L.0234; sign '2-2i' for '2i-2' at L.0605; index ranges at L.0195/0201; 'v_i' for 'x_i' at L.0485; 'n' for '2g' at L.0483; 'H^{i-6}' for 'H^1' at L.0738; 'c=1' for 'c=-1' at L.0756 and L.0687; '(c(w),w)' for '(-c(w),w)' at L.0766; 'n-3' for 'i-2' at L.0787; 'g>0' for 'g>1' at L.0647; 'A_{i,j}' for 'C_{i,j}' at L.0300; 'j' for 'i' at L.0826; missing predicate at L.0818). In every case the surrounding derivation, or a downstream use of the same object (e.g. L.0799 uses the correct exponent i-2 that L.0787 mis-states; L.0768 uses the correct sign that L.0766 mis-states), makes the intended and correct statement unambiguous. The density and uniformity of these slips indicates authorial sloppiness in the LaTeX source rather than a single substantive defect; none of them changes a quantitative conclusion.

One statement is literally over-broad rather than merely typographical: Lemma 'metabelian_injectivity' (L.0531-0535) asserts ad(v): gr_i(Lbar) -> gr_{i+1}(Lbar) is injective for all nonzero v in V_0 and all i, which fails at i=1 because ad(v)(v)=0 (e.g. free metabelian on V_0 = Q_p^2: gr_1 has dim 2, gr_2 = wedge^2 V_0 has dim 1). However the statement is correct for all i>=2 (there [L,L] is a torsion-free module over the polynomial ring and ad(v) is multiplication by a nonzero linear form), and every application (L.0560, L.0627, L.0689) only needs 'infinitely many i', so i>=2 suffices; at i=1 the argument also survives by choosing v outside W^{c=-1}. This is a repairable over-statement, not a failure of the proof.

I therefore found no step that definitively fails, and report VALID.
